focus: Overlay, copy-on-write, sandbox, and one-worktree write redirection
noveltyJustification: Separated filesystem byte sharing from Git metadata ownership and traced the exact-attribution boundary through explicit git -C roots, shared dependency links, checkout watch behavior, and churn sampling.
ruledOut: one-worktree environment-only write redirection as exact attribution
shared Git metadata or a shared overlay upper/work pair
unregistered copy-on-write directories as a replacement for git worktree move

label: COW saves bytes only when each lane owns a private upper/work view and Git metadata
One-worktree environment redirection is not exact under explicit git -C and shared cwd seams
COW does not reanchor dependency self-links or repair compiled entry-point realpath guards
Git move survives only for registered worktrees; arbitrary overlay and sandbox mount contracts need external relocation repair
The status scanner and the lane must name the same physical or mounted root for attribution to be exact
Shared immutable lower or object bytes are compatible with isolation; shared mutable upper, index, or worktree metadata is not
No setup, apparent-disk, changed-block, or six-lane COW benchmark was run; packet worktree measurements remain the only observed cost baseline

reason: Lifecycle Git calls strip redirectors and the shared-checkout watch is report-only, so the design cannot assign all writes exactly.

direction: shared overlay upper/work or shared Git index
reason: A shared mutable layer collapses the status and write ownership boundary; OverlayFS documents upper/work as per-mount state.

direction: unregistered COW directory for Git move semantics
reason: Git move/repair applies to registered linked worktrees, not arbitrary mount or sandbox metadata.
